title: Handelman's integrability conjecture for log-convex functions
statement:
Let $h:(0,\infty)\rightarrow(0,\infty)$ be a log-convex function satisfying

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{h(n)}{h(n+1)}=1.
$$

Assume that $h^2(x)/h(2x)$ is integrable on $(0,\infty)$. **Handelman's integrability conjecture.** Then $h$ is also integrable on $(0,\infty)$. Handelman posed this question in connection with maximal functions and the integrability of products involving log-convex functions; the supplied text does not establish whether the conjecture is resolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10970

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).
source_name: Brian Simanek, “On Some Convexity Questions of Handelman”, arXiv:2402.10970 (2024).
